commitResults.messageTitle: Changed name to CHOO and added greetings
echo commands entered by the user, exit when type 'bye'
added commands for list and add
Use custom exceptions for input errors

commitResults.messageBody: Store deadline values as LocalDateTime and accept strict date-only or date-time input. Preserve explicit midnight through storage, report legacy free-form data clearly, and update documentation and regression tests.
Move command input and all user-facing output into a cohesive Ui class. Inject streams for focused testing while preserving the existing console transcript exactly.
Represent user input as typed parsed commands and move syntax validation and task construction into Parser. Keep CHOO focused on dispatching actions while preserving all existing errors and output.

Encapsulate collection ownership and one-based position validation in TaskList. Convert CHOO into an instance coordinator over Ui, Parser, TaskList, and Storage while retaining rollback on save failures.

Group application, parser, storage, task, UI, and exception classes by responsibility under the choo package. Mirror the test layout, teach the UI runner to compile recursively, and update the documented launch path.

Point the application plugin at the packaged CHOO entry point and document Gradle build and run commands. Allow the pre-JUnit test sources temporarily so the Gradle build succeeds in the required increment order.
Require affected JUnit tests to be updated after Java changes and focus coverage on the highest-value non-trivial methods.

Convert the highest-value parser, storage, task, UI, and application scenarios to JUnit 5 so Gradle discovers and runs them automatically. Remove the temporary allowance for builds with no discovered tests.
Explain how to build, locate, test, and release the executable CHOO JAR while keeping generated binaries out of version control.
Explain command rollback, parsing validation, storage encoding, strict date conversion, and task-position contracts. Document public enum constants so the Javadoc build completes without warnings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use standard Java naming and layout
commitResults.messageBody:
The Java sources use inconsistent import grouping and an all-uppercase
entry-point class name.

Rename the entry point to Choo, standardize imports and Javadocs, and
update its build and README references without changing behavior.

Future Java changes need a reusable summary of the course rules.

Add a validated project skill that routes Java work through the SE-EDU
basic and intermediate standard and the project verification steps.

Future commits need consistent messages that the course dashboard can
recognize.

Add a validated project skill for focused commits, imperative subjects,
and useful what-and-why bodies based on the SE-EDU conventions.

The starter guidance does not capture the grading-sensitive iP
workflow or the standards that future work must follow.

Record the project safeguards and require agents to load the Java
and Git standard skills before relevant code and commit work.

Users cannot locate related tasks without reading the complete list.

Add a find command that searches task descriptions by keyword and shows
matching tasks in their original order. Document and test empty,
case-sensitive, and description-only searches.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/choo/parser/CommandType.java
#	src/main/java/choo/parser/Parser.java
#	src/main/java/choo/task/TaskList.java

Indent switch labels and wrapped declarations according to the SE-EDU
Java coding standard. Improve the Choo class header so its purpose is
clear without changing behavior.

Replace ambiguous schedule, storage, parser, and UI identifiers with
names that explain their roles. Keep command behavior, persistence, and
output unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs to initialize task lists

commitResults.messageBody: Add a dark theme and original profile avatars to give CHOO a clearer product identity. Improve message styling and verify that GUI resources are packaged correctly.

Command execution assumes that parsing and task loading have completed.
Task-list operations also depend on every stored task being non-null.

Document these internal contracts with Java assertions so programming
errors fail close to their source without replacing user-facing error
handling. Add focused tests for the task-list null checks.

Storage parsing combines field validation, task construction, and status
restoration in one method. This makes each storage rule harder to inspect
and maintain independently.

Separate validation and task creation into focused helpers, and use pattern
matching when serializing task subtypes. This keeps each method at a single
level of abstraction without changing the persisted format.

Task searching and storage serialization transform task collections using
manual loops. The loop mechanics obscure the filtering and mapping intent.

Use stream pipelines to express both transformations directly. Preserve
task order and immutable search results while keeping the existing storage
format and command behavior unchanged.
Add assertions for task invariants
Improve storage parsing readability
Use streams for task transformations

Console output mixes fixed LF characters with platform line separators.
This causes otherwise valid output assertions to fail on Windows CI.

Build the banner and test expectations with the platform line separator so
console output remains consistent on every supported operating system.

Task order depends only on insertion order, which makes approaching
deadlines difficult to identify in a mixed task list.

Add a sort command that places deadlines in stable chronological order
before undated tasks. Save the reordered list and document its behavior,
including regression coverage for ordering and storage failures.

Conversation bubbles use a fixed width, and error responses look like
ordinary replies. This makes long output harder to read and important
failures easy to miss.

Make bubble widths respond to the window size, reduce the avatar
footprint, and give errors a distinct high-contrast style. Keep the
existing commands and console output unchanged.
Improve GUI feedback

CHOO's replies and interface use a generic assistant voice, so the
product has little identity beyond its name.

Adopt a calm railway stationmaster theme across greetings, task
confirmations, errors, and the GUI header. Keep commands and task
behavior unchanged while making the wording concise and consistent.
Give CHOO a stationmaster personality

Some malformed commands currently fall through to generic errors or let
repeated schedule delimiters become task data. This makes corrections
unclear and can create unintended tasks.

Reject blank commands, arguments on no-detail commands, and repeated or
misordered schedule delimiters. Recognize only standalone delimiter tokens
so delimiter-like description text remains valid.
Handle malformed command structures

Core command, storage, parser, and UI formatting paths still have
untested branches, while no automated threshold prevents regressions.

Add focused JUnit cases for those paths and integrate JaCoCo reporting.
Enforce 95% line and 90% branch coverage for non-GUI code, leaving JavaFX
rendering to manual smoke tests as allowed by the increment.
Expand automated test coverage

The README does not identify reused foundations or widespread AI
assistance, leaving the project's reuse disclosure incomplete.

Record the course foundation, build and test tooling, Codex assistance,
and AI-generated avatar assets so their origins are transparent.
Document project acknowledgements

The guide lacks startup and recovery instructions, and the product
website is not configured for GitHub Pages.

Explain setup, commands, and storage recovery. Configure the Pages
theme and link the published guide from the project README.
Publish the CHOO user guide

The guide covers commands but lacks quick navigation and explicit
outcomes for first-time users. Search-result numbering can also be
mistaken for full-list task numbers.

Add navigation, a command summary, and troubleshooting examples.
Explain task numbering and immediate deletion to help users avoid
unintended changes.

The release JAR includes only Intel macOS natives. A Java runtime
with JavaFX installed hides this, while plain Java on Apple Silicon
fails to initialize the renderer.

Bundle universal macOS libraries without changing application code.
Check both architectures and GUI resources in the finished JAR so
CI catches this packaging regression on every build platform.
Document the supported platforms and plain-Java release checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the product screenshot and smoke-test record
commitResults.messageBody:
The product guide lacks a representative image of the released GUI.
Command tests alone cannot establish that the standalone JAR renders
correctly or reloads saved tasks through the interface.

Add a full-window capture with realistic tasks and record the GUI
checks. Explain the runtime modules needed for isolated testing so
an incomplete test runtime is not mistaken for an application bug.

Integrate the polished guide, full-window screenshot, and verified
Apple Silicon packaging after local and three-platform CI checks.
Keep application commands unchanged and preserve the release test record.
